\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Logspace.PreimageHost}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Machine simulation phases]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.Ph}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.Ph}
\leanok
The phase set consists of the phases ask, bit, zt, iC, iB, dD, dL, dE, and dB, together
with phases $\mathrm{work}(a,lb)$ for each optional Boolean value $a$ and Boolean value $lb$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Index of the added work tape]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.q}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.q}
\leanok
For a machine with $k$ work tapes, let $q$ denote the last index among the $k+1$ work
tapes, namely the index $k$ of the added tape.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Next simulation phase]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.nextPh}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.nextPh}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.Ph}
Given an input-head movement $d\in\{-1,0,1\}$ and Boolean values $lb,rb$, choose the
next phase as follows: if $lb$ is true, choose ask when $d=1$ and otherwise choose
work$(\mathrm{none},\mathrm{true})$; if $lb$ is false, choose zt when $d=-1$, choose
iC when $d=1$ and $rb$ is false, and choose ask in all other cases.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Action extended with a simulation phase]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.liftAct}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.liftAct}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.Ph, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.nextPh, Turing.Action}
Given a machine action $A$ and Boolean values $lb,rb$, form an action for one additional
work tape and a state paired with a phase. The input head stays still, the original
work-tape actions and output are preserved, and the new tape is left blank with its head
stationary; if $A$ has a successor state $s'$, the new successor is
$(s',\mathrm{nextPh}(d,lb,rb))$, where $d$ is the input-head movement in $A$, and if $A$ halts,
the extended action also halts.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Simulation transition function]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.tr}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.tr}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.Ph, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.liftAct, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.q, Complexity.LogProg.decDAct, Complexity.LogProg.decEAct, Complexity.LogProg.decLAct, Complexity.LogProg.incBAct, Complexity.LogProg.incCAct, Complexity.LogProg.junkAct, Complexity.LogProg.regAct, Turing.Action}
For a Boolean-symbol machine $M$, define a transition function on pairs of states and
phases, with an optional input symbol and the symbols scanned on its $k+1$ work tapes.
In phase work$(a,lb)$, apply $M$'s transition using the first $k$ scanned symbols and
the optional symbol $a$, then extend its action using $lb$ and taking $rb$ to be true
exactly when $a$ is absent and $lb$ is false. In phase zt, leave the added tape
unchanged and stationary, moving to work$(\mathrm{none},\mathrm{true})$ if that tape
is blank and to dD otherwise. In phases iC, iB, dD, dL, dE, and dB, perform the
corresponding counter action on the added tape: iC increments it, iB advances its head
left over nonblank cells and right at a blank, dD decrements it while choosing dD or dL
according to the scanned bit (and moves left to dB at a blank), dL moves left to dE at a
blank and to dB otherwise, dE writes a blank and moves left to dB, and dB uses the same
head movement as iB. The counter actions use the scanned bit to choose their specified
write and successor behavior. In phases ask and bit, the transition halts without
changing any tape.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Oracle call specification]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.call}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.call}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.CallSpec, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.Ph, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.q}
For a machine state $s$, define a call specification as follows: in phase ask, call
decider $0$ in whole-input mode with the added tape as its sole argument, continuing in
phase bit after a positive answer and in phase work$(\mathrm{none},\mathrm{false})$
after a negative answer; in phase bit, call decider $1$ in whole-input mode with that
same sole argument, continuing in phase
work$(\mathrm{some}\,\mathrm{true},\mathrm{false})$ after a positive answer and
phase work$(\mathrm{some}\,\mathrm{false},\mathrm{false})$ after a negative answer.
In every other phase, there is no call.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Oracle-interacting simulation program]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.prog}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.prog}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.Ph, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.call, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.tr, Complexity.LogProg.RProg}
For a Boolean-symbol finite-tape Turing machine $M$, define a program with $k+1$ work
tapes, two possible deciders, and states paired with simulation phases. Its initial
state is $(q_0,\mathrm{ask})$, where $q_0$ is the initial state of $M$; its ordinary
transition function is the simulation transition function, and its call function is the
oracle call specification described by the phase.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Initial simulator configuration]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.start}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.start}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.Ph}
For a finite-tape Turing machine $M$ with Boolean tape symbols, the initial
configuration of its log-space simulation is the pair consisting of $M$’s initial state
and the phase “ask.”
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Lower tape-position bounds]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.lo}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.lo}
\leanok
For a finite-tape Turing machine $M$ and a natural number $S$, define a lower-bound
function on its $k+1$ tape positions by assigning the value $-1$ to the final position
and $-S$ to every earlier position.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Upper tape-position bounds]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.hi}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.hi}
\leanok
For a finite-tape Turing machine $M$ and natural numbers $S,W$, define an upper-bound
function on its $k+1$ tape positions by assigning $W$ to the final position and $S$ to
every earlier position.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Simulated configuration encoding]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.imageCfg}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.imageCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.Ph, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape}
Let $M$ be a finite-tape Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, let $v$ and $x$ be
finite Boolean strings, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $v$. For a
natural number $i$ and a simulation phase $p$, define the corresponding configuration on
input $x$ to have state $c$’s state paired with $p$ when $c$ is nonhalting, input-head
position $1$, an added work tape containing the buffer representation of the binary
expansion of $i$, the original work tapes, an added work-head position $0$, the original
work-head positions, and the original output string.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Representation by a simulated configuration]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.Represents}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.Represents}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.Ph, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.imageCfg, Turing.Cfg}
Let $M$ be a finite-tape Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, let $v,x$ be finite
Boolean strings, let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $v$, and let $d$ be a
configuration of the simulator on input $x$. Say that $d$ represents $c$ if there is a
natural number $i\leq |v|$ such that $d$ is the simulated encoding of $c$ using index
$i$ and phase “work” with no Boolean value and flag true when the input-head position of
$c$ is $0$, and phase “ask” otherwise; moreover, if $c$ is nonhalting, then $i$ equals
its input-head position minus one.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Safety conditions for simulator configurations]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.Safe}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.Safe}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.Ph, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.hi, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.lo, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.prog, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.q, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape}
Let $M$ be a finite-tape Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, and let $x$ be a
finite Boolean string. For natural numbers $F,S$, a simulator configuration $d$ on input
$x$ is safe if every work-head position lies between its prescribed lower bound (with
parameter $S$) and upper bound (with parameters $S$ and the length of the binary
expansion of $F+1$); and whenever $d$ is in a state whose program entry is a call, the
input-head position is $1$, the head on the distinguished tape is at $0$, and that tape
contains the buffer representation of some natural number $i\leq F$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Safety of an encoded configuration]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.imageCfg_safe}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.imageCfg_safe}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.Ph, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.Safe, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.hi, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.imageCfg, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.lo, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.q, Turing.Cfg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $x,v$ be Boolean words, and let $c$ be a
configuration of $M$ on input $v$. Suppose $i\le |v|$, and every work-tape head of $c$
lies between $-S$ and $S$. Form a configuration for the compiled program on input $x$ by
retaining $c$'s state, output, original work tapes, and work-head positions, adjoining
one extra tape containing the binary expansion of $i$ with its head at $0$, placing the
input head at position $1$, and adjoining the phase $\mathrm{ph}$ to the state. Then
every work-tape head lies between its prescribed lower and upper bounds (the original
tapes between $-S$ and $S$, and the extra tape between $-1$ and the length of the binary
expansion of $|v|+1$); moreover, whenever the state is a call state, the input head is
at position $1$, the extra-tape head is at $0$, and that tape contains the binary
expansion of some integer at most $|v|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[One-step query transition]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.ask_step}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.ask_step}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.call, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.imageCfg, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.prog, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.q, Complexity.LogProg.regWords, Complexity.LogProg.rrun, Complexity.LogProg.rrun_one, Complexity.LogProg.rstep, Complexity.LogProg.tapeWord_bufferTape, Complexity.LogProg.vword_whole₁, Turing.Cfg, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a Boolean multitape Turing machine, let $x$ and $v$ be finite Boolean words,
and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $v$ whose state is $s$. For any natural
number $i$ and any oracle $o$ assigning a Boolean answer to each of the two query
indices and each Boolean word, one step of the compiled program from the encoded
configuration with phase ask leaves the encoded machine configuration and the auxiliary
register contents unchanged. Its resulting phase is bit if $o$ answers true on query
index $0$ and the pair encoding of $x$ with the binary expansion of $i$; otherwise the
phase is work with no pending write and a false left-boundary flag.
\end{theorem}

\lean{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.bit_step}

\begin{theorem}[Replacing the encoded index tape]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.index_view}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.index_view}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.Ph, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.imageCfg, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.q, Complexity.LogProg.regCfg, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $x,v$ be Boolean words, and let $c$ be a
configuration of $M$ on input $v$ whose state is $s$. For any natural numbers $i,j$ and
phases $\mathrm{ph},\mathrm{ph}'$, first form the encoded configuration from $c$ with
index $i$ and phase $\mathrm{ph}$, then set its state to $(s,\mathrm{ph}')$, replace the
extra tape by the tape containing the binary expansion of $j$, and put that tape's head
at position $0$. The resulting configuration is exactly the encoded configuration from
$c$ with index $j$ and phase $\mathrm{ph}'$.
\end{theorem}

\label{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.adjust_index}

\uses{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.Ph, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.Represents, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.Safe, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.imageCfg, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.imageCfg_safe, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.index_dec, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.index_inc, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.nextPh, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.prog, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.zero_step, Complexity.LogProg.moveInputPos_val, Complexity.LogProg.rrun, Complexity.LogProg.rrun_add, Turing.Cfg, Turing.moveInputPos}

Let $M$ be a Boolean multitape Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $x$ and $v$ be
input words, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $v$ whose state is $s$.
Suppose its input-head position is obtained by moving a position $p$ by sign
$m\in\{-1,0,1\}$, and every work-tape head of $c$ lies between $-S$ and $S$. Then there
is a number of steps $T$ such that the compiled program, started from the encoding of

phase set according to the head movement and whether $p$ is an endpoint, reaches an

determined by $S$ and the binary length of $|v|+1$; whenever the compiled program is at
a query state, its input head is at position $1$, its extra-register head is at position
$0$, and that register contains the binary expansion of some integer at most $|v|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Work-tape head bounds from space]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.source_head_bounds}

\begin{theorem}[Simulation with a bounded counter tape]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.run}

\uses{Complexity.LogProg.OIS.Represents, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.Safe, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.hi, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.imageCfg, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.lo, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.prog, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.q, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.represented_step, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.represents_safe, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.source_head_bounds, Complexity.LogProg.OIS.start, Complexity.LogProg.rrun, Complexity.LogProg.rrun_add, Complexity.LogProg.rrun_zero, Turing.Cfg.init, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.MultiTapeTM.exists_first_halt, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{6}
Let $M$ be a Boolean multi-tape Turing machine, and let $x$ and $v$ be Boolean words.
Suppose an oracle $o$ satisfies, for every $i\le |v|$, $o_0(\langle
x,\operatorname{bits}(i)\rangle)$ is true exactly when $i<|v|$, and, for every $i<|v|$,
$o_1(\langle x,\operatorname{bits}(i)\rangle)$ equals the $i$th bit of $v$ (with false
as the default). If $M$ halts on input $v$ after $t$ steps, then the compiled oracle
program, started on input $x$, halts after some $N$ steps and produces the same output
as $M$. At every time $n\le N$, each ordinary work-tape head lies between $-S$ and $S$,
where $S$ is the space used by $M$ through step $t$, while the additional tape head lies
between $-1$ and $L$, where $L=|\operatorname{bits}(|v|+1)|$; moreover, every oracle
call made before step $N$ begins with input-head position $1$ and additional-tape head
position $0$, and that tape stores $\operatorname{bits}(i)$ from cell zero for some
$i\le |v|$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $M_0,M_1$ be finite Boolean Turing
machines, and let $A_0,A_1$ be languages of Boolean words. Suppose that each $M_j$
decides $A_j$ with space bound $s_j$. For Boolean words $x,v,w$, assume that for every
$i\le |v|$, the encoding of $x$ paired with the binary expansion of $i$ belongs to $A_0$
if and only if $i<|v|$, and for every $i<|v|$, that encoding belongs to $A_1$ if and
only if the $i$th bit of $v$, taken to be false when absent, is true. Suppose that $M$
on input $v$ halts after $t$ steps with output $w$, and that $B$ is a natural number
such that, for both $j=0,1$ and every $i\le |v|$, the maximum of $s_j$ at the length of
the encoded input and $1$ is at most $B$. Then the compiled machine constructed from $M$
and the two deciders halts on input $x$ with output $w$ at some time $T$, and its space
usage by time $T$ is at most
$M.k\bigl(2\,\mathrm{space}_M(v,t)+1\bigr)+\bigl(|\mathrm{bits}(|v|+1)|+2\bigr)+2K(2B+1)$,
where $K$ is the maximum number of work tapes of $M_0$ and $M_1$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{6}
Let $f$ map finite binary strings to finite binary strings, and suppose its output
length is bounded by $C(|x|+1)^c$ for some natural numbers $C,c$. Suppose also that each
of the following languages is in $\mathsf{LOGSPACE}$: the language of pairs $(x,i)$ for
which the $i$th bit of $f(x)$ is $1$, and the language of pairs $(x,i)$ for which
$i<|f(x)|$, with pairs represented by the encoding that doubles the bits of the first
string, appends the separator $01$, and then the second string. Then for every language
$A\in\mathsf{LOGSPACE}$, the language $\{x:f(x)\in A\}$ is in $\mathsf{LOGSPACE}$.
\end{theorem}
